# Independent audit: joint complements and original-cap grouping

Audited `candidate fd71224e218c86d2` in full.
Result: **PASS**; no correction identified. The exact verifier
`supporting computation verify_joint_complement_group_constants.py` also passes.

The common remainders retain every strict cap-complement inequality.
Their positive-volume compact inner approximants admit the stated
Minkowski interpolation; dimension at the integer target forces the
q-dimensional source direction spaces to agree before intrinsic
Brunn–Minkowski is applied. The separate q=0 argument is valid.

On each fiber, a finite closed union covering almost everywhere
covers the entire convex body, including its relative boundary.
Finite Helly applies to the open convex complement pieces in the
q-dimensional affine hull. The resulting groups have at most q+1
unchanged original caps. Their positive joint-remainder supports
are lattice-convex, so Doignon selects at most 2^n groups. Empty
support sets, vertical caps, and closed boundary mass cause no gap.

The added Section 2.1 also passes. Strict superlevels above the
attained finite max-min value remain lattice-convex, including the
zero-level case. Their empty common intersection admits a Doignon
subfamily of at most 2^n sets. This gives the reverse max-min
inequality with an actually attained subfamily. Dividing each group
remainder by its own fixed positive constant preserves the required
individual superlevel property.

The quantitative threshold proof uses actual union masses. Its
strict summation has at least one strict positive-part contribution
when the threshold budget is positive; the zero-budget branch is
handled separately. A common surviving fiber for all groups is
not mistaken for a common surviving point for all original caps.

The overlap identity counts repeated original caps with their
occurrences. The spanning-tree inequality is pointwise correct:
the induced active subgraph has at most h−1 edges when h vertices
are active. The uniform pair-overlap estimate retains the correct
signs and constants. The interval calibration is exact.

In the simplex-product sharpness example, each cap is isolated to
its own binary base, and every barycentric cap is uniquely needed
near its corresponding simplex vertex. This forces q+1 caps per
owned fiber and 2^n groups. The planar pairwise remainder fractions
5/9 and 2/9 are correct, while the strict three-cap remainder is
empty. This last example properly limits pairwise extrapolation.

The note gives exact group selection and overlap-sensitive bounds.
It does not prove a universal positive overlap charge or a gamma_q
allocation. In particular it adds actual cover information beyond
separate scalar majorant inequalities; the obstruction in
`candidate 3bbe467275a530f8`
does not rule out exploiting this additional information.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
